title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Procedures, and Top Support Issues
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Overview:

This page consolidates Developer Experience (DevEx) standards and canonical content for SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the top support issues with canonical fixes. Use this as the single source of truth for authors and maintainers producing customer-facing developer docs and internal quickstarts.

Purpose:
- Standardize structure and tone across SDK guides and quickstarts so that developers can onboard to Redwood Inference in under 30 minutes.
- Surface canonical API examples (REST, streaming, embeddings) that are kept up-to-date by the Docs Owners rotation.
- Provide an operating procedure for docs-site changes (PR process, release cadence, and emergency fixes).
- Document the top support issues observed by DevEx and Customer Support along with reproducible fixes and mitigations.

Scope:
- Applies to: SDK guides (Python, Node, Go), quickstarts, API examples, docs-site content and templates in eng-developer-experience.
- Excludes: product PRDs, internal engineering design documents (see eng-platform), and experimental notes (store those in Google Drive).

Ownership and Roles:
- Docs Owner (primary): DevEx Docs team (rotating on a 6-week cadence).
- Secondary reviewers: SDK maintainers (Python/Node/Go), API platform team, Security.
- Publishing lead: DevEx Release Manager.

Doc Metadata Standards (table):
| Field | Expected value | Example |
| Title | Short, descriptive, dash-separated filename | developer-experience-sdk-quickstart-python-2026 |
| Space | eng-developer-experience | eng-developer-experience |
| Author | Full name | Ava Thompson |
| Owner team | engineering | engineering |
| Status | draft | published |
| Labels | 0-8 tags | devex, sdk, quickstart |

File Naming and Location Conventions:
1. Place quickstarts and templates under: /eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/.
2. Filenames: lower-case, dash separated, include year or date when relevant (e.g., sdk-quickstart-python-2026-03-04.json).
3. Use the doc title metadata to be user-facing and the filename for machine sorting.

Content Structure for SDK Guides and Quickstarts (required sections):
- Title and short blurb (1-2 sentences).
- Prerequisites (account, API key, environment variables, minimum SDK version).
- Quick installation + hello-world (copy-paste).
- Detailed example(s) (one end-to-end: auth -> request -> response handling -> error handling).
- Best practices and common pitfalls.
- Troubleshooting & top support issues (link back to this page).
- Changelog / compatibility notes.

Quickstart Template (canonical):
---
Title: Redwood Inference SDK Quickstart \u2014 Python
Blurb: Get started with Redwood Inference in under 5 minutes using the Python SDK.
Prerequisites:
- Redwood account and API key
- Python 3.9+
- pip install redwood-inference-sdk>=1.5.0

Installation:
```bash
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
pip install redwood-inference-sdk==1.6.2
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...
```

Hello world (Python):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ["REDWOOD_API_KEY"])
resp = client.text.generate(model="redwood-chat-1", prompt="Summarize Redwood's mission in one sentence.")
print(resp.text)
```

Notes:
- Include expected latency and token limits for the example model. e.g., redwood-chat-1: 2\u20134 token/ms at sequence length 256 on Hosted.

API Examples (canonical set \u2014 keep these minimal and copy-paste ready):
1) REST (cURL) \u2014 text generation:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","input":"Write a haiku about latency."}'
```
2) Python (streaming example):
```python
for chunk in client.text.stream(model="redwood-chat-1", prompt="Explain prefix caching"):
    print(chunk.delta, end="", flush=True)
```
3) Embeddings (Node example):
```js
const {Redwood} = require('redwood-sdk');
const r = new Redwood(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY);
const emb = await r.embeddings.create({model: 'redwood-embed-1', input: 'Customer support triage'});
console.log(emb.embedding.length);
```

Docs Site Operating Procedures (DOCS-OPS):
- Branching and PRs:
  1. Create a docs branch: docs/<area>/<short-desc> (e.g., docs/sdk/python-quickstart-fix).
  2. Update JSON doc in the correct directory (use the canonical template).
  3. Add reviewers: @devex, @sdk-maintainer.
  4. Run the docs validator (docs/ci/validate-docs.sh) \u2014 this checks metadata and schema.
  5. Merge when two approvals are present.
- Release cadence:
  - Weekly content release on Tuesdays at 09:00 PT (automated deploy via CI).
  - Emergency/patch releases allowed for critical fixes (see emergency procedure).
- Emergency procedure (example):
  1. Create a hotfix branch: docs/hotfix/<short-desc>.
  2. Reach out to on-call Docs Owner and API on-call via #docs-ops with link to PR.
  3. Mark PR with label: hotfix-critical and request expedited review.
  4. After merge, trigger manual site redeploy (docs/ops/redeploy-manual.sh) and post an incident note if customer-facing breaking issue.

Docs Validation Checklist (pre-merge):
- Metadata: title, space, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated present and valid.
- Content: code blocks runnable and pinned to versions where applicable.
- Links: no broken internal links (run link-checker).
- Accessibility: images have alt text and examples include short captions.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (current top 8):
1) Issue: API 401 when using stored token in CI.
   Symptom: curl returns 401; SDK raises AuthenticationError.
   Root cause: Token rotation disabled or env var not set in CI job.
   Triaging steps:
     - Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY present in CI environment.
     - Check secrets provider (Vault/Secrets Manager) rotated token timestamp.
   Fix: Re-inject updated API key; update CI secret reference to use the non-rotating service token or implement token refresh logic.
   Preventive doc link: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/ci-auth-and-api-keys-2025

2) Issue: Large payloads causing 413 / timeouts in upload path.
   Symptom: Client receives 413 or connection reset when sending long prompt (>60k chars).
   Root cause: Gateway/body size limit or model config mismatch.
   Fix: Use chunked uploads for file payloads, or switch to embeddings endpoint (for document indexing) and reference batching guidance. Update quickstart to show chunking example.

3) Issue: Streaming responses delayed / arriving in big chunks.
   Symptom: Developer expects incremental tokens but receives full output after delay.
   Root cause: User-level buffering (HTTP client) or SDK default buffer settings.
   Fix: Add streaming notes to SDK guides and example for event-driven streaming clients; include recommended client config (e.g., axios: {responseType: 'stream', decompress: false }).

4) Issue: Unexpected price spike after moving to Dedicated.
   Symptom: High token cost and high GPU usage.
   Root cause: Autoscale config set to aggressive burst; model variant selection fallback to larger model.
   Fix: Guide customer to pin model versions and set burst limit in Dedicated config; add a Runtime note in quickstart about cost controls.

5) Issue: Embeddings mismatch between SDK and REST examples.
   Symptom: Different embedding vector lengths returned from two clients.
   Root cause: Different model parameter (model vs model_version) or older SDK pinned to previous embedding model.
   Fix: Standardize examples to include full model identifier and show version pinning; add tests in docs CI to compare lengths across sample inputs.

6) Issue: CORS errors in browser quickstarts.
   Symptom: Browser console shows blocked by CORS when calling hosted API directly.
   Root cause: Direct client-side API key usage and missing browser proxy.
   Fix: Update quickstart to show using server-side proxy or Redwood Edge proxy configuration; emphasize never embedding API keys in frontend.

7) Issue: SDK compatibility break on new major release.
   Symptom: Examples that previously worked throw TypeError after SDK bump.
   Root cause: Breaking API change in new major version.
   Fix: Pin SDK versions in quickstarts; add migration notes and a small compatibility table in SDK guides.

8) Issue: Poor default output quality after quantized model selection.
   Symptom: Customer sees hallucinations after switching to 4-bit quantized model.
   Root cause: Quantization profile not appropriate for the prompt distribution.
   Fix: Document recommended quantization profiles per workload; include guidance in quickstart for testing quality vs. cost and a rollout plan.

Canonical Fix Template (for support articles and PRs):
- Title: Short descriptive issue name
- Symptom: Short bullet list of observable symptoms
- Root cause: One-line root cause
- Repro steps: Minimal reproduction (cURL, SDK snippet).
- Fix: Step-by-step fix with commands and expected verification.
- Mitigation: Short-term workaround if full fix requires infra change.
- Owners: Support + SDK + Platform owners (add slack handles).

Publishing Checklist (post-merge):
- Validate site build in staging and click through examples.
- Smoke tests (run docs/ci/run-examples.sh).
- Update changelog and release notes.
- Notify #devex-updates with link to change and short summary.

Maintenance and Rotation:
- Docs Owner rotation schedule (6 weeks): maintainers file issues for updates and triage weekly backlog in Sprint planning.
- SDK maintainers perform quarterly walk-throughs of examples to ensure compatibility with the latest SDK release.

Appendix: Useful snippets and links
- Docs validator: docs/ci/validate-docs.sh
- Example quickstart repo: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-quickstarts

If you are updating an existing quickstart, please link to this page in the "Troubleshooting" section and add the canonical support issue ID (SUP-####) when relevant.
